age.evidence: Forty-three (43) male Long Evans rats (N = 24, 227 ± 12 g, for experiment 1; and N = 19, 268 ± 24 g, for experiment 2)

dosing.evidence: Groups of (n = 6) rats received either saline, harmine (1 mg/kg), DMT (1 mg/kg), or harmine + DMT (1 mg/kg each) as subcutaneous injections... N = 19 rats received an injection of saline (n = 14) or harmine (n = 5) at a dose of 3 mg/kg (s.c.), followed 5 minutes later by DMT at a dose of 3 mg/kg.
harmine (1 mg/kg)... harmine + DMT (3 mg/kg each); dissolved in EtOH containing fumaric acid (1 mg/mL) and then diluted 1:10 with PBS

group_housing.evidence: Housing was in groups of four in individually ventilated cages

day_night_flipped.evidence: 12-h light/dark cycle (lights were on from 6 a.m. to 6 p.m)

enrichment_housing.evidence: environmental enrichment, which consisted of wooden sticks, bedding and a red-colored shelter

judge_notes: All three candidates returned zero behavioural assays. This is correct: the paper is a pharmacokinetic / PET / ex vivo receptor occupancy study. The endpoints are brain drug concentrations (HPLC-MS), ex vivo [3H]ketanserin and [18F]MH.MZ binding (receptor occupancy via tissue scintillation/gamma counting), and [18F]FDG-PET cerebral glucose metabolism under isoflurane anesthesia — none of which are behavioural assays per the rubric (PET imaging without a behavioural task is explicitly excluded).

The authors note in passing that they observed head-twitch responses in some rats, but state they 'did not systematically assess behavioral indices' — no HTR data were collected or analyzed, so no HTR assay is scoreable.
Vehicle coded as 'other' (10% EtOH/PBS, with fumaric acid in experiment 2) since the primary solvent is an ethanol/PBS mixture rather than a single standard vehicle.
